title: Microsoft Edge: top sites in the Edge search bar
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts and both policy controls are supported by Microsoft's current documentation. The registry paths flagged by the pre-check are documented, and the updated policy index does not contradict the briefing; the feature's default, licensing and rollout details remain unstated.

claims.claim: The two policy pages describe no setting that governs only the search-bar top-sites list.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edge search bar" "top sites" "hide" policy; read both quick-links pages and current policy index. These policies also govern new-tab quick links; SearchbarAllowed controls the whole search bar, not only its top-sites list.

claims.claim: The policy pages do not document a setting that prevents individual users from hiding search-bar top sites.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge search bar top sites prevent users hiding dedicated policy browsing history; "Edge search bar" "top sites" "hide" policy. Read both quick-links pages: mandatory tiles cannot be deleted, but preventing hiding is not stated.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes top sites as a list users act on themselves and describes no action taken on their behalf.
claims.quote: Adding easy access to top sites in Edge search bar on desktop. Users can add, edit, remove, or hide top sites. Admins can control available to this feature using the NewTabPageManagedQuickLinks and NewTabPageQuickLinksEnabled policies.
